summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Pteridophytes are seedless Tracheophytes with xylem tracheids and phloem sieve cells. Their free-living photosynthetic prothallus requires water for zooidogamous fertilization.

conceptBreakdown.content: Pteridophytes (*Pteris* = fern) are the First Vascular Land Plants (**Tracheophytes**). They are seedless, spore-bearing plants (**Vascular Cryptogams**) that possess fully differentiated vascular tissues (xylem and phloem).

conceptBreakdown.heading: 5.1 Dominant Sporophyte & Vascular Anatomy
conceptBreakdown.title: 5.1 Dominant Sporophyte & Vascular Anatomy
conceptBreakdown.content:
1. **Dominant Generation**: The main plant body is an independent, autotrophic, dominant diploid Sporophyte ($2n$), differentiated into true roots, stems, and leaves.

2. **Vascular Architecture**:
- **Xylem**: Consists exclusively of tracheids (true xylem vessels are **ABSENT**, except in rare genera: *Selaginella*, *Equisetum*, and *Marsilea*).
- **Phloem**: Consists exclusively of sieve cells (companion cells are **ABSENT**; albuminous cells present).

conceptBreakdown.heading: 5.2 Stelar Evolution in Pteridophytes
conceptBreakdown.title: 5.2 Stelar Evolution in Pteridophytes
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
STELAR EVOLUTIONARY TREND
                            
    PROTOSTELE                 SIPHONOSTELE                DICTYOSTELE
 (Solid Core Xylem)  ──►   (Central Pith Ring)   ──►   (Dissected Bundles)
 ├── Haplostele            ├── Ectophloic              └── Overlapping Leaf Gaps
 ├── Actinostele           └── Amphiphloic                 (True Ferns)
 └── Plectostele               (Soleno/Siphonostele)
conceptBreakdown.content:
The stele is the central vascular cylinder of the stem and root, comprising xylem, phloem, pericycle, and pith (if present).

1. **Protostele (Primitive Solid Stele)**: Central solid core of xylem surrounded completely by phloem; **pith is ABSENT**.
- **Haplostele**: Smooth, circular xylem core (*Rhynia*).
- **Actinostele**: Star-shaped xylem core with radiating arms (*Lycopodium serratum*).
- **Plectostele**: Xylem core broken into parallel plate-like strands (*Lycopodium clavatum*).

2. **Siphonostele (Medullated Stele)**: Central core of parenchymatous pith surrounded by vascular tissue.
- **Ectophloic Siphonostele**: Phloem lies only on the outside of xylem (*Equisetum*).
- **Amphiphloic Siphonostele**: Phloem rings lie on both outer and inner sides of xylem (*Marsilea* rhizome).

3. **Solenostele**: Siphonostele with non-overlapping leaf gaps.

4. **Dictyostele**: Stele dissected into multiple isolated vascular strands (**meristeles**) by numerous overlapping leaf gaps (*Dryopteris*, *Pteris*).

conceptBreakdown.heading: 5.3 Gametophyte Generation (The Prothallus)
conceptBreakdown.title: 5.3 Gametophyte Generation (The Prothallus)
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
PTERIDOPHYTE LIFE CYCLE
                           
     SPOROPHYTE (2n) ──[Meiosis]──► Spores (n) ──► Germination ──► PROTHALLUS (n)
            ▲                                                          │
            └─────── [Syngamy] ◄── Antherozoid + Egg ◄── [Antheridium / Archegonium]
conceptBreakdown.content:
Sporangia produce haploid spores via meiosis. Germinating spores produce an inconspicuous, small, free-living, photosynthetic, thalloid gametophyte called a **Prothallus**.

• **Prothallus Requirements**: Requires cool, damp, shady places to survive, restricting the geographical distribution of pteridophytes.
• **Fertilization (Zooidogamy)**: Water is required for the flagellated antherozoids (biflagellate in *Selaginella*, multiflagellate in ferns) to swim to the archegonium venter.
